summary: Comprehensive testing of the new community auth layer (cookie/bearer-based social login). Backend: 9/9 pytest tests pass — providers listing (google + session_ttl_days=7), /me 401 without creds, /me with cookie, /me with Bearer, bad token → 401, /session with invalid session_id → 401 (not 500), /session with disabled provider 'microsoft' → 400 with clear detail, /logout invalidates session (next /me returns 401), admin JWT login regression works. Frontend: 17/17 Playwright checks pass — /join renders all 5 provider buttons (google clickable; microsoft/linkedin/apple/facebook show PRONTO badge), authenticated /join redirects to /, authenticated home shows header-profile-name + avatar + left-sidebar-name/avatar and hides join CTAs, profile dropdown menu opens with logout, logout completes and unauth CTAs reappear, /capital + /executive-summary + /investor-pitch-deck all render (HTTP 200) and /admin/login page still loads. No regressions detected.

issues: authService.me() logs '401 Failed to load resource' on every anonymous page load. Functionally correct (401 → user=null) but noisy; consider suppressing via a HEAD-style check or catching before console reports it.

critical_code_review_comments: authService.me() surfaces a browser 'Failed to load resource: 401' console error for every unauthenticated pageview — expected behavior semantically, but pollutes DevTools. Suggest a probe endpoint returning 200+{authenticated:false} or catching fetch error at network layer.
Cookie flags default to secure=true unless COOKIE_SECURE=false; correct for prod but ensure local VS Code dev docs mention it (playbook already covers).
AuthCallback uses processed useRef guard for double-invocation — good; keep as-is.
Community routes exclude password_hash and _id from user projection — good.
SESSION_TTL_DAYS module-level constant read only at import time; providers endpoint re-reads env each request — inconsistent but harmless.

Provider registry correctly exposes only 'google' as enabled (microsoft/linkedin/apple/facebook return 400 with clear detail). Frontend correctly shows PRONTO badges on disabled providers and full authed UI (header profile menu, sidebar avatar) when cookie present. Admin JWT auth coexists without conflict.
